AGENT EVALUATION · TECHNICAL REPORT · NOVEMBER 2026

CardShopBench

Evaluating autonomous agents in a
capital-constrained resale economy

Vedant Bhatter Independent research & engineering
Results & analysisCodeExperiment data

Abstract

Operating a resale business requires decisions whose consequences unfold over time: capital spent today becomes inventory, inventory must find a buyer, and revenue arrives only after settlement. CardShopBench provides a reproducible environment for studying these decisions through an eight-tool agent interface. A frozen universe of 75 Pokémon card price references initializes a 30-day simulation with explicit fees, shipping, delivery delays, and cash constraints. We evaluate three deterministic baseline policies over 135 episodes spanning three market scenarios, three execution regimes, and five paired seeds. The report examines strategy sensitivity through equity trajectories, bootstrap intervals, and transaction-level replay. A provider-compatible model harness supports subsequent language-model evaluations; the experiments reported here establish the environment's baseline behavior.

BASELINE VALIDATION

These are executed rule-based strategies, not AI model scores. They validate the environment before model comparisons. Prices begin with real observations; subsequent price paths, purchase opportunities, and buyer demand are synthetic.

Intervals reflect five simulated market seeds, not real-world forecasting uncertainty. Small-sample intervals are exploratory. Strategies have direct access to public scenario prices; LLMs use the tool interface.

Research question

How sensitive is a purchasing policy to execution friction and market shocks when all policies face the same exogenous market events?

Controlled comparison

Each configuration shares its initial capital, card universe, episode length, and five random seeds. Event-keyed randomness prevents tool-call ordering from changing the market path.

Interpretation

Equity includes estimated inventory liquidation. Positive equity returns do not establish realized cash profitability, and the demand model is a simulation assumption rather than a fitted market model.

BENCHMARK DESIGN

Environment and evaluation protocol

The agent chooses its actions. The environment owns the ledger. A persuasive explanation cannot create a sale, erase a fee, or spend money twice.

Every episode uses integer-cent accounting, delivery and settlement delays, a daily action budget, and deterministic market events. Matched seeds expose each strategy to the same opportunities.

◇

Evidence before confidence

Source timestamps and card variants stay attached to observations. Forum claims are research evidence, never transaction ground truth.

⌁

Stress the assumptions

Reprint and hype scenarios test capital discipline. Three execution regimes expose sensitivity to demand and liquidation discounts.

▤

Make failures inspectable

Tool actions, invalid requests, purchases, sales, and settlements are recorded. Checkpoints preserve environment state.

Execution assumptions and limitations

Baseline defaults: 13.25% illustrative selling fee, $4.50 outbound shipping, $1 inbound cost, two-day delivery, two-day settlement, and 12 actions per simulated day. These are configurable assumptions, not verified fees for a specific marketplace.

Daily sale probability is capped at 85% and decreases exponentially with asking price relative to the scenario reference. Conservative/base/optimistic demand multipliers are 0.55/1.0/1.4; inventory liquidation uses 65%/75%/85% of the scenario reference before selling costs. None is calibrated to observed sell-through.

Current references aggregate unspecified card conditions. This release does not benchmark graded-card valuation, low-pop scarcity, negotiation, returns, counterfeit detection, actual local transactions, or historical forecasting. No live model API calls were made for the published baseline results.

Data selection favors 25 higher-priced eligible variants per selected set ($5–$500), so results are not representative of the entire Pokémon market. The universe is frozen; any future historical study must address survivorship and training-data leakage.
